subject: Private deployment: egress matrix + next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthsuite.io>, Rachel Lowe <rachel.lowe@healthsuite.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: private deployment egress & PII handling

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful discussion and great context on HealthSuite's requirements. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key constraints you shared
- Air-gapped/offline option preferred for PHI-sensitive flows (clinical transcripts).
- No general internet egress from the VPC. Outbound must be strictly limited to approved endpoints via VPC endpoints/NAT with customer-controlled firewall.
- Retention: minimum 30 days for logs, but PHI artifacts must be configurable for shorter retention and automatic purge.
- Audit: detailed request/response logging with customer-managed keys for encryption at rest (KMS/HSM).

Our immediate asks (to validate feasibility)
1) Confirm whether HealthSuite can accept egress to a customer-controlled S3-compatible endpoint in the same region (VPC endpoint) for model telemetry and batch logs.
2) Clarify specific ports/protocols allowed for outbound (e.g., HTTPS 443 only, or allow specific IP ranges).
3) Which environments must be air-gapped vs. allowed to have controlled egress (prod only? staging?): label them (prod/stage/dev).

Next steps we propose
- We’ll produce an "egress matrix" mapping Redwood outbound endpoints to recommended VPC controls and port rules. (Draft attached: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx)
- Technical deep-dive with your infra/security team next week to walk the ingress/egress map and confirm blocked/allowed endpoints.
- If air-gap is required for a subset of flows, we’ll propose an on-prem package with one-way import/export and manual model updates.

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx (checklist & initial mapping)

Questions from our side before the deep-dive
- Can you share the preferred SIEM ingest method (syslog, HTTPS collector, other)?
- Do you have an existing HSM/KMS provider we must integrate with, or should we propose options?

Thanks — I’ll hold a draft calendar invitation for Wed/Thu next week but happy to move to a time that works for your infra team.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0162

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthsuite.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Lowe <rachel.lowe@healthsuite.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: private deployment egress & PII handling

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing with infrastructure: 

1) Air-gap: for production clinical workloads we need the option for an "isolated" deployment that has zero outbound internet access. That may require an on-prem appliance or a VPC with no NAT and a manual data import/export process.

2) Egress allowed: if we must allow any outbound, it must be strictly to an S3-compatible endpoint inside our VPC (via Gateway or Interface endpoint). No DNS-based allowlisting (we prefer IP ranges + endpoint IDs).

3) Ports/protocols: HTTPS (443) only. No outbound SSH or other control-plane ports.

4) Logging: we can accept syslog over TLS to our collector; alternatively we can host an HTTPS ingestion endpoint on-prem. All logs containing PHI must be tagged and retained per our retention policies, but we want config knobs to drop PHI from logs after X days (we’ll propose retention window in a follow-up).

One other ask: can Redwood run with customer-managed encryption keys (Bring-Your-Own-KMS) for persistent storage of request/response artifacts?

We’re available for a technical call Tue 6/16 or Thu 6/18 — prefer mornings.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure | HealthSuite
alex.johnson@healthsuite.io

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: private deployment egress & PII handling

Alex — thanks for the clarifications. We’ll align internally and come back with a technical sketch and a conservative egress matrix that satisfies the "no internet" requirement for prod + limited egress for non-PHI telemetry in staging.

Karthik / Dev — can you take point on the sketch? Karthik, please include:
- Minimal outbound endpoints (DNS + IP ranges if required) and whether VPC Interface or Gateway endpoints fit each case
- Options for BYOK/KMS and HSM integration (which key flows require customer KEKs)
- A recommended logging architecture (syslog over TLS to HealthSuite SIEM, or short-lived token push to your HTTPS endpoint)

Alex — I’ll propose Tue 6/16 09:30 PT for the deep-dive; if that works I’ll send calendar invite.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthsuite.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: private deployment egress & PII handling

Alex / team — attaching a first-draft ingress/egress map and an egress matrix (ingress-egress-map.pdf). High-level summary below; full notes in the PDF.

Summary (first-pass) - Production (PHI): fully isolated VPC with no NAT. Data flows:
  * Inbound: customer uploads (s3-compatible endpoint) only via pre-signed artifacts or staged media (one-way import).
  * Outbound: none. No internet egress. Model updates delivered manually or through an approved air-gap process.

- Staging (non-PHI telemetry allowed): limited outbound to customer-controlled S3 endpoint via Interface VPC Endpoint (HTTPS 443). No DNS wildcard allowlisting; we'll enumerate endpoint IDs and IP ranges where required.

- Telemetry & logging:
  * PHI artifacts: encrypted with customer KEK (BYOK); logs containing PHI are tagged and routed to your syslog TLS collector in-region via a VPC endpoint. Retention configurable (we’ll build the purge job).
  * Non-PHI metrics/telemetry: aggregated and optionally forwarded to your external observability stack via controlled egress.

- KMS/HSM: Redwood can support CMAK/BYOK patterns. For strict HSM requirements we can integrate with your on-prem HSM through an approved connector; we'll include the integration effort estimate in the follow-up doc.

- Ports/protocols: HTTPS (443) only outbound for allowed flows; no SSH or other control-plane egress.

Attachments: ingress-egress-map.pdf (technical sketch), redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx (checklist)

Action items
1) Alex: confirm whether HealthSuite prefers Interface vs Gateway VPC endpoint for S3-compatible storage, and send any IP ranges for allowlisting.
2) Stephanie/Marissa: confirm calendar for Tue 6/16 09:30 PT and share dial-in.
3) Dev/Karthik: prepare a short runbook for air-gap model updates and an estimate for manual update cadence.

If Alex confirms 6/16 09:30 PT I’ll send a meeting invite and upload the two attachments to the shared Drive link.

Thanks — Karthik
